cases.given: A fresh database is prepared through the existing shared SQLite setup, including its standalone and server initialization paths.
cases.when: Initialization completes and a valid ticket is inserted without an explicit ticket ID.
cases.then: The tickets table is available through each path, no ticket or parent row was seeded by initialization, and the inserted ticket has a usable INTEGER primary-key identity.

cases.given: Prepared SQLite connections have existing users, categories and services, and a ticket with otherwise valid required values.
cases.when: Each required reporter, category or service reference is omitted, NULL or supplied as an absent parent ID; each optional technician, verifier or closer reference is omitted, NULL, supplied as an existing user ID or supplied as an absent user ID.
cases.then: Missing, NULL and absent-parent required references are rejected; omitted and NULL optional references are stored as NULL; existing optional user references are retained; absent optional user references are rejected.

cases.given: A prepared database has the parent rows needed for a valid ticket.
cases.when: Tickets are inserted with each required description, impact or urgency omitted or NULL; with each supported impact and urgency value and one unsupported value; and with priority omitted, NULL, each of P1 through P4 or an unsupported value.
cases.then: Missing or NULL required inputs and unsupported structured values are rejected; supported inputs persist, and omitted or NULL priority persists as NULL without a calculated default.

cases.given: A prepared database contains a service with a current business criticality and the parent rows needed for a valid ticket.
cases.when: A ticket is inserted with the caller-supplied service criticality omitted, NULL, each supported value or an unsupported value, and the referenced service's business criticality is later changed.
cases.then: Missing, NULL and unsupported ticket criticality values are rejected; supported supplied values persist as independent ticket snapshots and remain unchanged after the service update.

cases.given: A prepared database has the parent rows and other required inputs for a ticket.
cases.when: Tickets are inserted without created_at, without status, with explicit NULL status, with each supported status and one unsupported status; later lifecycle timestamps and both summaries are omitted, NULL or populated.
cases.then: Missing creation time, NULL status and unsupported statuses are rejected; omitted status persists as open, supported explicit statuses persist, and optional event timestamps and both summaries persist as NULL or their supplied values without requiring event-field correlation.

cases.given: A prepared database contains a ticket with otherwise valid inputs.
cases.when: The response and resolution deadline fields are left omitted or NULL, then populated with calculated values; existing stored values are read again without an explicit ticket update.
cases.then: Both deadline fields can persist independently as NULL or supplied stored values, and stored values remain stable without a recalculation on read.
